fieldNotes.truckGate: No controlled truck entrance. The truck court wraps the W, N and E faces and connects to the surrounding street network by open paved driveways. z19 satellite of every entry point and 2020-era Street-View on Sunset Blvd and the SE service road show no barrier arm, no sliding gate, no guard booth and no perimeter fence. Open-access urban infill DC.
fieldNotes.guardShack: No staffed booth anywhere on the truck circulation.
fieldNotes.remoteGs: False — requires a gate; there is none.
fieldNotes.postGateStaging: Wide paved truck courts on the W and N sides give ample interior holding before the docks.
fieldNotes.drivewayLong: The truck courts run the full building length; easily hold 3+ truck queues.
fieldNotes.entryExitSeparate: Truck circulation enters and leaves the wrap-around court at more than one point on different building faces (W dock court, N drop yard) rather than through a single shared gate group.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: Large facility with dock banks on the W/SW face and the N face; combined door count estimated ~70 — `dockDoors` 50+.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Two distinct drop-trailer concentrations — a N-face drop yard and a long E-face trailer row — both full of trailers without tractors; `dropArea` 50+, `dropYard: true`.
fieldNotes.shipRcvSeparate: Two physically separate dock clusters on different building faces (W/SW and N) suggest split shipping/receiving; medium confidence from overhead imagery only.
fieldNotes.buildingCount: Main DC plus a separate 2-story glass office building at the W end of the property.
fieldNotes.railServed: No rail spur enters the property.
fieldNotes.urbanRural: Dense Rocklin (Sacramento metro) setting — apartments to the north, single-family residential to the east, retail/industrial to the south and west; Urban per rubric.
fieldNotes.truckGateCount: Two open truck-court access points (no gate structures); counted as truck entrances per the metric definition.
